prompt: In GKE Standard, who runs etcd for your cluster?
hint: Which half of the cluster is it in?

choices.text: You, on a node pool reserved for it
choices.why: etcd is part of the control plane, which never appears in your project.

choices.text: Google
choices.why: Right. The control plane, etcd included, is Google's to run and patch.

choices.text: A Compute Engine VM created in your project with the cluster
choices.why: No control-plane machine appears in your project.

choices.text: Nobody: GKE replaces etcd with Cloud SQL
choices.why: GKE does not swap etcd for Cloud SQL; it runs the control plane for you.

prompt: A zonal cluster's zone has an outage. What happens to pods that were already running on nodes in other zones?
hint: What does the API server do, and what does it not do?

choices.text: They stop at once, because nodes need the API server to run anything
choices.why: Running pods keep running; the kubelet does not need the API server second by second.

choices.text: They keep running, but nothing is scheduled, scaled or changed
choices.why: Right. The control plane is unreachable, so the cluster is frozen rather than down.

choices.text: GKE moves the control plane to a healthy zone within seconds
choices.why: That is what a regional cluster gives; a zonal one has one control plane.

choices.text: They are rescheduled into the healthy zones
choices.why: Rescheduling needs the scheduler, which is in the unreachable control plane.

prompt: The cluster management fee is 0.10 USD an hour. What do three clusters cost for a month of 730 hours, before any credit?
hint: Fee times hours times clusters.

prompt: A cluster whose location is a region, such as southamerica-east1, is a ___ cluster.
hint: Not zonal.

prompt: Why does gke/main.tf have no node pool in it?
hint: What does the cluster resource describe?

choices.text: GKE Standard creates its nodes from the cluster's machine type
choices.why: The cluster resource has no machine type for its nodes here; pools carry that.

choices.text: Nodes are added later by hand with kubectl
choices.why: kubectl does not create Compute Engine nodes.

choices.text: A regional cluster cannot have a default pool
choices.why: Regional clusters do have pools; this file simply keeps them separate.

choices.text: The pools are a resource of their own, in pool.tf
choices.why: Right. The cluster resource describes the control plane, and each pool is managed separately.

prompt: A regional pool covers three zones with autoscaling min_node_count = 1 and max_node_count = 3. What is the largest number of nodes it can reach?
hint: The bounds are per zone.

prompt: The shop's pool says node_count = 1. How many e2-standard-4 machines does it start with?
hint: How many zones does the region have?

choices.text: One, the number written in the file
choices.why: In a regional cluster the count is per zone.

choices.text: Zero, until a pod is scheduled
choices.why: node_count is the starting size; autoscaling bounds come from min and max.

choices.text: Three, one in each zone of the region
choices.why: Right; about 293 dollars a month at the floor.

choices.text: Nine, the maximum of the autoscaling bounds
choices.why: Nine is the ceiling, not the start.

prompt: What is a node pool underneath?
hint: Lesson 4 builds one of these by hand.

choices.text: A managed instance group of Compute Engine machines
choices.why: Right. GKE drives the group for you.

choices.text: A Kubernetes Deployment of nodes
choices.why: Nodes are machines, not pods in a Deployment.

choices.text: A Cloud Run service with one revision per node
choices.why: Cloud Run is not involved in GKE nodes.

choices.text: A set of App Engine flexible instances
choices.why: App Engine flexible is a different product.

prompt: The shop wants photo resizing, which can be interrupted, kept off the nodes that serve customers. What is the usual shape?
hint: Pools exist for kinds of node.

choices.text: A second cluster just for the batch work
choices.why: That works and adds a second management fee for no reason a pool cannot meet.

choices.text: A larger machine type for the existing pool
choices.why: Bigger nodes still mix both workloads.

choices.text: A higher max_surge so batch pods get the surge nodes
choices.why: Surge nodes exist only during upgrades.

choices.text: A second pool of Spot nodes with a taint the batch pods tolerate
choices.why: Right. Only tolerating pods land there, and Spot suits interruptible work.

prompt: Match each setting in pool.tf to what it does.
hint: Three of them are in management and node_config.

pairs.right: Replaces a node that fails its health checks
Moves nodes to versions the release channel offers
Pods ask GKE's metadata server, not the node's account
The starting number of nodes in each zone

right_distractors: Sets the maximum pods per node

prompt: In what order does GKE upgrade a cluster?
hint: The API server supports nodes behind it, never ahead.

choices.text: The control plane first, then the node pools
choices.why: Right. Nodes may lag the API server by some minor versions, never lead it.

choices.text: Nodes first, then the control plane
choices.why: Nodes ahead of the API server is the one order not supported.

choices.text: Both at once, to keep them on one version
choices.why: They are upgraded in sequence.

choices.text: Whichever pool has the most nodes, then the rest
choices.why: Pool size does not set the order.

prompt: A pool has max_surge = 1 and max_unavailable = 0. What is true during its upgrade?
hint: One adds, one removes.

choices.text: Capacity drops by one node at a time, to save money
choices.why: max_unavailable = 0 means it never drops.

choices.text: One extra node exists at a time, and capacity never drops
choices.why: Right. Slower, and you pay for the extra node while it exists.

choices.text: All nodes are replaced together after one extra is added
choices.why: Surge replaces in small steps; replacing a whole set is blue-green.

choices.text: Pods are not evicted, because there is spare capacity
choices.why: Every old node is drained; spare capacity is where its pods go.

prompt: Order the release channels from the one that receives new versions first to the one that keeps a version longest.
hint: Extended goes past standard support.
trap: EXTENDED is not a slower STABLE: it keeps a minor version past standard support, at an extra fee during that period.

prompt: A Deployment with one replica goes down for a minute every time the nodes are upgraded, although max_unavailable is 0. Why?
hint: What does max_unavailable count?

choices.text: max_unavailable is ignored on the regular channel
choices.why: The setting applies on every channel.

choices.text: The control plane is down during node upgrades
choices.why: The control plane is upgraded first and separately.

choices.text: It counts nodes, and the one pod still restarts when its node drains
choices.why: Right. Two replicas and a PodDisruptionBudget keep the service up.

choices.text: Surge nodes start without the image cached
choices.why: A slow pull lengthens the gap; it does not explain why there is a gap at all.

prompt: Before an old node is removed, GKE cordons it and then ___ it, evicting its pods.
hint: The word kubectl uses for the same thing.

prompt: Which of these did the lab check when you ran terraform validate on lesson 13's files? Choose all that apply.
hint: Enum values are known to the provider.

choices.text: That the release channel is one of the accepted names
choices.why: Right; WEEKLY was refused.

choices.text: That the upgrade strategy is one the provider knows
choices.why: Right; ROLLING was refused.

choices.text: That an upgrade would keep every pod running
choices.why: Nothing was upgraded; pods are not even in the files.

choices.text: That the maintenance window allows 48 hours in 32 days
choices.why: That rule is checked by GKE when the cluster is created.

prompt: The window's start_time is 05:00 UTC. What time is that in São Paulo?
hint: São Paulo is three hours behind UTC.

choices.why: That is where the window ends, at 11:00 UTC.

choices.text: 05:00, because GKE converts to the cluster's region
choices.why: The times are UTC; nothing converts them.
That would be two hours behind.
Right; date with TZ=America/Sao_Paulo printed it.

prompt: GKE asks for 48 hours of maintenance availability in any 32 days. With a window on Saturdays and Sundays only, how many hours long must each day's window be, at least?
hint: Count the fewest weekend days any 32 days can hold.

prompt: Which exclusion scope suits "nothing changes on the nodes during a two-month migration"?
hint: One scope is limited to a short period.

choices.text: NO_UPGRADES, renewed every few weeks
choices.why: That scope is limited in length, and renewing it piles up a large upgrade.

choices.text: NO_MINOR_OR_NODE_UPGRADES
choices.why: Right. The narrower scopes may last much longer, up to the end of support.

choices.text: A maintenance window of zero hours
choices.why: A window has to leave 48 hours in 32 days.

choices.text: The EXTENDED release channel on its own
choices.why: A channel decides versions, not when nodes may change.

prompt: An exclusion with scope NO_UPGRADES is open, and the cluster's version reaches the end of its support. What happens?
hint: Two things go through regardless.

choices.text: The cluster is upgraded anyway
choices.why: Right. An exclusion chooses the moment; it does not keep a cluster still.

choices.text: Nothing until the exclusion closes
choices.why: End of support is one of the two things a window cannot hold back.

choices.text: The cluster is deleted
choices.why: Nothing is deleted; it is upgraded.

choices.text: The cluster moves to the EXTENDED channel by itself
choices.why: Changing channel is your decision, never automatic.

prompt: The recurrence FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=SA,SU is an RRULE, the syntax of the i___ standard.
hint: The same one a calendar invitation uses.

prompt: A regional cluster pays its 73 USD fee and keeps three e2-standard-4 nodes at 97.84 a month each. What is the monthly total?
hint: Fee plus three nodes.

prompt: Order what happens in one surge step of a node upgrade.
hint: Capacity first, then removal.
items: A node at the new version is created
Its pods are evicted, respecting PodDisruptionBudgets
trap: Cordoning before the new node exists is what max_unavailable = 0 prevents.

prompt: A team keeps one cluster per developer, eight in all, each a zonal cluster with one small node. Which line of their bill is the surprise?
hint: One cluster's fee is covered by the credit.

choices.text: The nodes, because zonal nodes cost more than regional ones
choices.why: A node costs its machine type, wherever it is.

choices.text: Egress between the clusters' control planes
choices.why: Control planes do not talk to each other.

choices.text: Seven management fees of about 73 dollars each
choices.why: Right. The credit covers one; the others add about 511 dollars a month before any node.

choices.text: Nothing, because zonal clusters are free
choices.why: Only one is covered by the credit.
